text:
deploy-bot: starting rollout v2026.04.2 -> prod

deploy-bot: rollout strategy = wave (US -> EU -> APAC). wave targets = US 30%, EU 40%, APAC 30%. change window 02:00-05:00 UTC. fallback pin: v2026.03.9. health checks enabled.

Maya: FYI I'm going to warm up routing and pre-cache KV for US slice. will run a quick QPS ramp to validate.

Rob: +1. I'll kick off smoke suite against the US pinned slice now.

Lucas: checking capacity reservations — US pool spare GPU slots = 6, baseline slots used = 14, expected additional = 4. spare margin ~20%.

Lucas: headroom metrics (live):
```
US-gpu-1: 72% mem, 58% util
US-gpu-2: 65% mem, 45% util
queue-len: 12 -> target < 20
``` 

Maya: perf target is p95 < 220ms for gen requests. we need at least 15% spare to avoid backpressure during ramp. Lucas can you reserve +2 slots for the wave? @SRE-Oncall

SRE-Oncall: reserving 2 slots in US pool now. Also enabling soft-evict on low-priority background jobs for the window.

Rob: smoke results: all checks green except rerank latency spike on one replica (175ms -> 310ms). re-running.

Rob: reran, looks like one transient noisy host. draining and replacing.

Maya: decision: proceed with US 30% wedge after 10m observation. rollback triggers: 5% error-rate sustained for 5m OR p95 latency > 350ms for 10m OR CPU>85% sustained 10m. fallback will pin traffic to v2026.03.9 automatically.

Anya: please add an alert to the deploy playbook channel if any rollback trigger fires. I can take handoff.

deploy-bot: US wedge set to 30% at 02:12 UTC. phased ramp steps: 5% -> 15% -> 30% every 2m with 4m observation windows.

Maya: observing metrics. p50 95ms, p95 180ms, errors 0.3%.

Lucas: still 2 spare GPU slots reserved. queue stable.

Rob: smoke pass complete. no downstream faults. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: moving to EU wave in 20m. prepping EU warmup. EU reserve check in 10m.

Maya: EU note — EU clusters have slightly shorter cold-starts but lower spare capacity, recommend EU wave start at 25% then jump to 40% if steady.

Lucas: EU pool spare = 4 slots, baseline used 18. allocating +1 slot (best-effort). if we see queue > 25 we throttle EU ramp.

SRE-Oncall: setting temporary quota guard on EU to 40% with throttle rule: throttle after 45s queue growth > 15%.

deploy-bot: EU wedge started at 02:35 UTC at 25%.

Maya: EU p95 205ms, errors 0.6% (still under threshold). hold for next observation.

Rob: noticed a small uptick on a downstream cache miss rate in EU — investigating TTLs. probably unrelated to model change.

Anya: confirming playbook ready for manual rollback: command to pin is below.

Anya: pin command:
```
# Pin to previous stable
redwoodctl rollout pin --version v2026.03.9 --region all
``` 

Maya: thanks. if EU stays green for 12m we can jump to 40%.

deploy-bot: EU ramp to 40% at 02:50 UTC.

Lucas: APAC capacity check: APAC reserved pools are in maintenance window starting 03:30 UTC, recommend we delay APAC full slice until maintenance end +10m.

Maya: agree. schedule APAC start at 03:50 UTC, warmup at 03:40.

Rob: final preflight notes: release notes updated, feature flags toggled for safe-mode, observability dashboards pinned.

SRE-Oncall: setting a temporary incident channel monitor to catch any cross-region error spikes and paging rules for ops.

deploy-bot: APAC warmup scheduled 03:40 UTC, full APAC wedge 03:50 UTC.

Maya: running final cross-region smoke at 03:45 — will report back in 5m.

Maya: cross-region smoke OK. APAC p95 220ms, errors 0.4%.

deploy-bot: APAC wedge engaged at 03:50 UTC to 30%.

Anya: monitoring, no alerts. metrics look stable across regions. queue lengths nominal.

Lucas: post-roll metrics: overall p95 = 195ms, global errors = 0.45%, cost delta within expected band.

Rob: created a short postmortem template in #eng-releases (no incidents) and linked release notes.

Maya: leaving the pin window open for 45m in case of late regressions. after that we'll mark release as stable.

deploy-bot: rollout complete. final state = live v2026.04.2 at 100% with fallback pin preserved until 04:35 UTC.

Maya: great work team. closing out — moving to ops handoff for tomorrow. :tada:
